paper.title: Oxygen-rich microporous carbons with exceptional hydrogen storage capacity

S1.label: CA-4600
S1.material_description: CA-4600: KOH-activated carbon from hydrothermally carbonised cellulose acetate (CA-hydrochar), activated at 600 C; oxygen-rich (22.8 wt% O by CHN), non-graphitic (ID/IG 0.85)
S1.purification_method: HCl wash (10 vol%, 500 ml) then deionised water to neutral pH; dried 112 C
S1.activation_method: KOH chemical activation, KOH/hydrochar ratio 4, 600 C for 2 h under N2, 3 C/min ramp
S1.functional_groups: COOH, C-OH and O-C=O identified by IR (3430, 1630, 1380, 1115, 1025 cm-1) and by O 1s / C 1s XPS peak fitting

S2.label: CA-4700
S2.material_description: CA-4700: KOH-activated carbon from hydrothermally carbonised cellulose acetate (CA-hydrochar), activated at 700 C; oxygen-rich (17.9 wt% O by CHN), non-graphitic (ID/IG 0.94)
S2.purification_method: HCl wash (10 vol%, 500 ml) then deionised water to neutral pH; dried 112 C
S2.activation_method: KOH chemical activation, KOH/hydrochar ratio 4, 700 C for 2 h under N2, 3 C/min ramp
S2.functional_groups: COOH, C-OH and O-C=O identified by IR (3430, 1630, 1380, 1115, 1025 cm-1) and by O 1s / C 1s XPS peak fitting

S3.label: CA-4800
S3.material_description: CA-4800: KOH-activated carbon from hydrothermally carbonised cellulose acetate (CA-hydrochar), activated at 800 C; oxygen-rich (20.6 wt% O by CHN), non-graphitic (ID/IG 1.00)
S3.purification_method: HCl wash (10 vol%, 500 ml) then deionised water to neutral pH; dried 112 C
S3.activation_method: KOH chemical activation, KOH/hydrochar ratio 4, 800 C for 2 h under N2, 3 C/min ramp
S3.functional_groups: COOH, C-OH and O-C=O identified by IR (3430, 1630, 1380, 1115, 1025 cm-1) and by O 1s / C 1s XPS peak fitting

S4.label: AX21
S4.material_description: AX21: Commercially available high-surface-area activated carbon used as a benchmark and to validate the authors' gravimetric method; ca. 50% of porosity from micropores (no numeric texture in the main article)

measurements.source_location: Table 2, p. 4 (uptake); texture from Table 2, p. 4 (BET area, t-plot micropore area, total pore volume at P/Po ~ 0.99, t-plot micropore volume); packing density from p. 8; gravimetric, Hiden XEMIS Intelligent Gravimetric Analyser; H2 99.9999% with molecular-sieve filter; degassed 200 C / 1e-10 bar / 4-6 h; dried 24 h at 80 C (Methods, p. 10)
measurements.notes: the paper states -196 C; recorded as 77 K per corpus convention. total uptake is not measured: the authors derive it from the measured excess by their eq. (1) using the sample's total pore volume and a NIST compressed-H2 density. this paper reports BOTH total and excess at the same sample, temperature and pressure; the two rows are one measurement expressed two ways and must never be averaged together. at 1 bar the paper reports total and excess as equal (3.1). PORE SIZE NOT STORED: Table 2's 'Pore size' column reports THREE NLDFT pore size distribution maxima per sample, not an average (footnote c: 'Pore size distribution maxima obtained from NLDFT analysis'). For this sample they are 6/8.5/12 A (0.6/0.85/1.2 nm). average_pore_diameter_nm holds a single central-tendency statistic, which the paper never computes, and it designates no maximum as principal - it calls the 6-7 A feature 'extra' relative to its cellulose-derived comparator. Recording one of the three would assert a selection the authors did not make. Note also that PoreDiameterMethod has no NLDFT member although PoreVolumeMethod does. pore_volume_method = t_plot describes micropore_volume_cm3_g only; total_pore_volume_cm3_g is a single-point value taken from the nitrogen uptake at P/Po ~ 0.99. Likewise surface_area_method = BET describes bet_surface_area_m2_g, while micropore_surface_area_m2_g is t-plot

measurements.notes: TEMPERATURE DEDUCED, NOT STATED: the sentence reporting this value gives no temperature. Assigned -196 C (77 K) because the paper states its H2 uptake measurements were performed at -196 C OR 25 C only (Methods; 'Our assessment conditions (-196 or 25 C, and 0-30 bar)'), and separately reports AX21 excess uptake at 20 bar and 25 C as 0.3 wt% (Fig. 8a, captioned 'at 25 C'), so 4.7 wt% excess at 20 bar cannot be the 25 C measurement. The 5.9 wt% total shares the 4.7 wt% value's clause; the 2.1 wt% at 1 bar shares its sentence and its comparison set (CA-4700's Table 2 values, footnote d: -196 C). This is a deduction from values the paper states, not a reading of a statement, and not a convention supplied from outside.
